defendant: Keno Kozie Associates, LTD (an Illinois corporation registered to do business in Ohio)
agreement: Grant Agreement, Program No. SFPN_2017_439275-WF, amended by an Amended Grant Agreement dated on or about June 12, 2018 that amended Section 2; the complaint refers to the two together as the "Grant Agreement." The agreement's own cover page gives an Effective Date of March 24, 2017 and describes the money as financial assistance "to invest in workforce training associated with Grantee's project."
agreement_date: Entered into on or about January 24, 2018 per paragraph 4 of the complaint; the attached agreement itself carries an Effective Date of March 24, 2017. Amended Grant Agreement on or about June 12, 2018.
program: The complaint never names a JobsOhio program. The attached agreement carries Program No. SFPN_2017_439275-WF and describes the use of funds as "workforce training."
amount_sought: $40,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees and costs. This is the full grant.
job_commitments: Create 36 new jobs at the Project Site (375 North Front Street, Columbus, OH 43215) with a payroll of at least $1,044,420.00, and train 36 employees with a Total Training Investment of $238,070.00. Metric Evaluation Date December 31, 2019; Metric Expiration Date December 31, 2021.
shortfall: The complaint does not state any job or payroll number the company actually reached. It pleads two breaches: failing to timely file Annual Reports showing satisfaction of the Metric Commitments under Section 6(b), and, "[b]ased upon information and belief," breaching Sections 5(c) and 9(c)(vii) "by ceasing and thereby failing to maintain operations at the Project Site through the Metric Expiration date of December 31, 2021."
repayment_quote: Section 5 (quoted at paragraph 6 of the complaint): "5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement. *** (a) Metric Commitment. Grantee must attain all Metric Commitments set forth on the first page of this Agreement no later than the Metric Evaluation Date. Once Metric Commitments have been met, Grantee shall maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date. *** *** (c) Remedy. If Grantee fails to satisfy its obligations under Section 5(a), Section 6(b), or to maintain substantial operations at the Project site during the Term, Grantee is in default of this Agreement and Grantor may seek the remedies provided to Grantor under section 9 of this Agreement. ***" || Section 6(b) (quoted in part at paragraph 7): "Failure by Grantee to submit any Annual Report shall be a default for which Grantor may terminate this Agreement as set forth in Section 9." || Section 9 (quoted at paragraph 8): "(b) Remedies: Following a default by Grantee, Grantor may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: *** (ii) Demand Repayment of Grant Funds. Grantor may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed. Grantee shall repay such Grant Funds within thirty (30) days after written demand by Grantor. (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies Grantor may have under this Agreement or applicable law." || Section 9(e) (quoted in part at paragraph 11): Defendant is liable for all of Plaintiff's "expenses, including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees, in connection with the enforcement of this Agreement."
remedy_named: "Remedy" (Section 5(c)) and "Remedies" / "Demand Repayment of Grant Funds" (Section 9(b)(ii)). No liquidated-damages clause is quoted and the words clawback and liquidated damages do not appear.
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. The Grant Agreement is Exhibit 1, the Amended Grant Agreement is Exhibit 2, and the July 14, 2022 breach/demand letter is Exhibit 3. The filed PDF is 15 pages: a 4-page complaint followed by the exhibits.
outcome: Voluntarily dismissed by JobsOhio. "PLAINTIFF JOBSOHIO'S NOTICE OF DISMISSAL WITHOUT PREJUDICE": "Now comes Plaintiff JobsOhio and hereby dismisses this action without prejudice." The case was terminated the same day. No judgment was ever entered, and no answer was filed. Thirteen days from complaint to dismissal.
amount_recovered: No filing states any amount recovered. The dismissal gives no reason and no terms.

notes: This is the fullest public record in the batch: JobsOhio attached the signed grant agreement itself, not just quotes from it. The cover page of Exhibit 1 is a one-page metrics table (Grant Funds, Program No., Effective Date, Metric Evaluation Date, Metric Expiration Date, No. of Jobs to be Created, Total Payroll to be Created, No. of Employees to be Trained, Total Training Investment). The remedy is discretionary throughout: "Grantor may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed." Nothing in the quoted text requires JobsOhio to claw anything back, and nothing sets a formula. The complaint pleads the central breach only "[b]ased upon information and belief." The amount in the complaint, $40,000.00, does not match the $640,000 recorded for this recipient in the project's grant file; the complaint sues on one grant agreement only and does not mention any other award.

defendant: Legacy Measurement Solutions, Inc., 3500 Parkway Rd, Brookfield Twp, OH 44403 (also served at 10077 Grogans Mill Rd, The Woodlands, TX)
agreement: Grant Agreement. The complaint calls it a Grant Agreement and attaches it as Exhibit 1.
program: The complaint never names a JobsOhio program. It describes the money only as "grant funds."
amount_sought: $300,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees and costs. This is the full grant.
job_commitments: Create and maintain 150 jobs at the project site (3500 Parkway Road, Brookfield Township, Ohio 44403), generate total payroll of at least $6.8 million, train 69 employees with an investment of $330,000.00 in that training, and provide and maintain a total fixed asset investment of $5.6 million. The complaint says these had to be met and maintained "within Metric Evaluation and Metric Expiration dates specified in the Grant Agreement" but does not give those dates in its text.
shortfall: The complaint states no number the company actually reached. Paragraph 5 says only that Defendant "breached the Grant Agreement by failing to satisfy the metric obligations set forth in the Grant Agreement, including failing to meet and maintain the job creation and payroll metrics."
remedy_named: No remedy is quoted. The complaint cites Section 9(b) by number only: "On June 18, 2018, JobsOhio notified Defendant that it had breached the Grant Agreement, and pursuant to Section 9(b) of the Grant Agreement, JobsOhio demanded that Defendant repay the $300,000.00 of grant funds it had received within 30 days of the date of the letter." The words clawback and liquidated damages do not appear.
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. The complaint attaches the signed Grant Agreement as Exhibit 1. The filed PDF is 12 pages: a 3-page complaint followed by the agreement.
outcome: Removed to federal court, then terminated in Franklin County. The Termination Entry of April 4, 2019 reads: "By order of this Court this case is hereby TERMINATED for the following reason: the Notice of Removal to federal court filed November 13, 2018, should have terminated this action." No judgment was entered in Franklin County and no answer was filed there.
outcome_date: 2019-04-04 (termination entry); the Notice of Filing of removal was docketed 2018-11-13.
amount_recovered: Nothing in the Franklin County file states any amount recovered. The case left this court, so its result is not on this docket.

notes: This complaint does not block-quote the agreement at all. It is three pages and names Section 9(b) without reproducing a word of it, which makes it the opposite of the Keno Kozie complaint filed four years later by the same firm. The provision is still readable here, because the agreement itself is attached. Read directly from Exhibit 1, page 6 of the agreement, Section 9(b) provides: "(b) Remedies. Following a default by Grantee, Grantor may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: (i) Discontinue Disbursements. If the Grant Funds have not been fully disbursed, Grantor may terminate any and all of Grantor's obligations under this Agreement, including the obligation to make further disbursements of Grant Funds. (ii) Demand Repayment of Grant Funds. Grantor may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed. Grantee shall repay such Grant Funds within thirty (30) days after written demand by Grantor. (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies Grantor may have under this Agreement or applicable law." Exhibit 1 also carries Section 9(c) Early Termination, whose clause (vii) is triggered where "Grantor has reason to believe Grantee has ceased operations at the Project site," Section 9(d) Remedies Cumulative, Section 9(e) Effects of Termination, and Section 9(f) Grantor's Expenses. The wording of the 2013 agreement's Section 9(b)(ii) is word for word the same as the wording the 2017 Keno Kozie agreement carries, so this is form language JobsOhio has used for at least nine years. Note that the complaint cites Section 9(b) while the Keno Kozie complaint cites Section 9(e) for attorney fees, where this agreement puts expenses at Section 9(f); the section letters shifted between versions of the form.
